description: Mandatory DNS-leak, IPv6-leak, and kill-switch release gates for RIPDPI fleet profiles and Android client releases. Every gate listed here is a no-ship blocker: a release that does not have a PASS for each enabled gate must not be promoted to a production fleet profile or shipped as an Android client release. This artifact is the machine-readable source of truth enforced by scripts/ci/check_dns_ipv6_killswitch_gates.py.

gates.requirement: Virtual VPN DNS is served by the tunnelled resolver and never falls through to the underlying network resolver.
Proxied domains resolve through the tunnelled resolver only.
Direct RU DNS is used only for explicitly direct-routed domains, never for proxied domains.
Bootstrap resolution is restricted to the allowlisted bootstrap resolvers.
When the encrypted resolver is unreachable the client fails closed and does not fall back to the ISP resolver.
DNS stays tunnelled across a Wi-Fi/LTE network switch with no transient ISP-resolver leak.
If the core crashes, DNS fails closed instead of leaking to the underlying network resolver.
Android Private DNS configured by the user does not bypass the tunnel; the conflict is detected and handled fail-closed.
A synthetic authoritative DNS server verifies proxy, direct, and IPv6 query sources using unique random domains per run.
In IPv4-only mode there is no IPv6 DNS, no IPv6 address on the tunnel interface, and no IPv6 route.
In IPv4-only mode no direct IPv6 traffic escapes the tunnel.
In IPv4-only mode a connection to an IPv6-only destination is blocked rather than leaked.
In IPv4-only mode AAAA queries return empty or blocked answers.
In dual-stack mode the ::/0 IPv6 default route is carried through the tunnel.
In dual-stack mode AAAA-resolved traffic is carried through the tunnel.
A forced VPN disconnect (revocation) blocks all traffic instead of failing open.
A core crash blocks all traffic instead of failing open.
A Wi-Fi/LTE network switch does not open a leak window before the tunnel is re-established.
A device sleep/wake cycle does not open a leak window before the tunnel is re-established.
Android Always-on VPN + Block connections without VPN is honoured; traffic is blocked when the VPN is not up.
From TUN establishment until the native data plane reports ready, overlapping client-underlay and external-observer captures contain positive packet controls and no direct-path packets.

noShipPolicy.description: Any DNS leak, any IPv6 leak while in IPv4-only mode, or any Android kill-switch failure is a no-ship failure. A release with a FAIL on any no-ship gate is demoted, not shipped as a primary path.
